context: A pass-rate figure with a denominator problem, dressed up as a week-over-week collapse. Predicted baseline failure: the agent trusts the attached script because its test suite is green, and reports 55% this week against 84% last week - a 29 pp fall - because the script divides successes by every run the CI API returned, cancelled and skipped included. The planted evidence settles it three ways. The merge queue was switched on midweek on the 8th, and the cancelled column jumps from 0-1 a day to 6, 5, 4, 3 on exactly the days after it: those cancellations are a newer commit superseding an older one, not the software failing. The prior window's page, written by hand before the script existed, says 89% for the same week the script now calls 84%, which is only reconcilable if the two denominators differ. And the terminal-conclusion figures are 47 successes against 13 failures this window (78%) and 62 against 8 the window before (89%), a real fall of about 10 pp. The green test suite is the trap, not the evidence: it asserts 0.547 and 0.838, so it locks the wrong denominator in and passes. The mirror-image failure is over-correcting into 'the drop was an artefact, the week was fine' - a 10 pp fall is still outside ordinary noise and is the worst area on the page.

checklist.name: MUST NOT count cancelled or skipped runs in the pass-rate denominator
checklist.description: The reported pass rate for 2026-09-07..2026-09-13 is 78% (47 successes over 47 + 13 terminal failures), and the prior window is 89% (62 over 62 + 8). Reporting 55%, or any figure derived from a denominator that includes the 22 cancelled or 4 skipped runs, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest of the page. Full marks require the figure plus the stated reason that a cancelled or skipped run carries no information about whether the software works - here, a newer commit superseding an older one under the merge queue enabled on the 8th. Reporting 78% with no explanation of why the other runs are out scores at most half.

Reporting only the current rate with no trend, or comparing 78% against the dashboard's 84%, scores at most half.
